Multi-ancestry placental xQTL analysis

Internal QC + R21 progress report

Bhattacharya Lab (analysis: S. Bresnahan; report generated with Biomni/Phylo)

2026-09-28

1 Executive summary

This report summarizes the multi-ancestry placental xQTL analysis: cohort-only genotype PCA on LD-pruned variants within each ancestry stratum, a conventional covariate set (first 5 genotype PCs + HCP factors + sex, gestational age, and cell-type fractions; maternal cell fraction excluded before correlation pruning at |r| > 0.9; HCP count optimized per ancestry × modality via module 25b; no covariate cap), a MAF ≥ 0.01 filter with a ≥ 5 minor-allele-count floor at the genotype intersection, Storey q-values (computed with the R qvalue package), and per-phenotype rank-based inverse-normal transformation of all modalities (isoform usage mapped as within-gene relative-abundance ratios; isoform expression as transcript-level TPM abundance). Mapping covers 36 ancestry × modality × layer cells (EAS n ≈ 280, EUR n ≈ 140).

Headline result: 14959 associations reach FDR ≤ 5% across the 36 ancestry × modality × layer cells. The primary eGene catalog (combined cross-modality layer) contains 1330 EAS and 2187 EUR eGenes at FDR ≤ 5%; per-modality grouped eGenes are the breakdown, and ungrouped phenotype-level hits are reported descriptively (Results). Strongest association per ancestry: EAS: PGM1 (expression, grouped layer, q = 6.1e-26); EUR: ERAP1 (alt_polyA, ungrouped layer, q = 5.6e-36).

Storey calibration estimates a signal fraction (π1) of 6–41% across cells. In high-signal cells Storey q-values are correspondingly more liberal than Benjamini–Hochberg (by up to the estimated π0); the per-cell comparison is in Diagnostics.

The splicing modality splits by ancestry. At its modality-matched HCP count (k* = 5; HCP count optimization), EUR splicing yields 500 FDR ≤ 5% eGenes — under expression-derived covariates the layer carried no detectable signal, so the EUR splicing null was a covariate-specification artifact, now resolved. EAS splicing remains near-null (5 eGenes, best q = 0.0026), its eGene yield is flat across the HCP grid (≤ 3 chr1 eGenes at every k), and its p-values depart only mildly from the null at the median (genomic-control λ = 1.28; Diagnostics). Three lines of evidence bear on the residual EAS null:

  1. The machinery detects splicing signal where it exists — the same pipeline and covariate machinery yield the EUR splicing catalog above at n ≈ 140, a higher detection floor (r² ≈ 0.19) than EAS (r² ≈ 0.10 at n = 280; Power analysis). A pure sample-power explanation is therefore insufficient for EAS: EUR splicing effects cleared a higher bar. The leading candidate is EAS-specific attenuation of the splicing phenotypes — EAS pools four cohorts spanning single- and paired-end protocols, and junction-level quantification is the most protocol-sensitive of the nine modalities.
  2. The EAS null is not a covariate artifact — eGene yield does not improve at any HCP count on the grid (HCP count optimization), and the mild median λ elevation with only a handful of FDR-significant hits is the signature of diffuse, individually weak effects rather than of residual confounding (which would inflate the median without bound) or of a dead layer (λ ≈ 1, no tail). The FDR-significant hits in the other modalities carry estimated r² of 0.00–0.77 — exactly the class of outsize effect the floor permits.
  3. Signal replicates across ancestries — cross-ancestry rank concordance of gene-level signal on the combined layer is Spearman ρ = 0.16 (top-100 overlap 25/100), with same-variant slope concordance 0.54 — the pattern expected of real, partially shared genetic regulation, not of artifact-driven signal.

Carrier-count caveat. A fraction of tested pairs retain < 5 minor-allele carriers in the mapping sample sets (EAS: 0 tests; EUR: 43174 tests; audit table below) — the MAC ≥ 5 floor was applied before outlier exclusion. Flagged tests should be discounted; no FDR-significant result should be carrier-limited.

2 Data and methods

2.1 Pipeline recap

  • Phenotypes: 9 RNA modalities (gene expression, isoform usage, isoform expression, splice junction usage, intron retention, alternative TSS, alternative polyA, RNA editing, RNA stability), harmonized to genotyped samples (array_id), with NIGMS technical replicates averaged per individual. The two isoform modalities are both built from QU-corrected Salmon transcript counts (mean count ≥ 10): isoform usage is within-gene relative-abundance ratios (transcript TPM / gene-total TPM; PANTRY convention, mean ratio in [0.05, 0.95]) and isoform expression is the pre-ratio transcript TPM abundance (devBrain §3.3 convention). Per ancestry stratum: feature filtering (isoform usage: usage > 0.1 in > 25% of samples; isoform expression: TPM > 0.1 in > 25% of samples, devBrain §3.3; ratio modalities: detected in ≥ 40%, devBrain §3.4), batch-median NA imputation, quantile normalization across samples + rank-based inverse-normal transformation per phenotype, then ComBat (batch = cohort) last — the devBrain “ComBat on the normalized data” convention. No log2 pre-transform is applied: rank-based INT is invariant to any monotone transform, so log2/VST would be exact no-ops on the mapped scale.
  • Genotypes: ancestry-stratified plink2 pgen; variants filtered to MAF ≥ 0.01 with MAC ≥ 5 (≥ 5 minor alleles) at the genotype intersection — the count floor excludes low-carrier tests, which can produce spurious associations, while MAF 0.01 keeps the variant pool as large as defensible. tensorQTL’s own MAF ≥ 0.01 filter applies on top at mapping time.
  • Genotype PCA: cohort-only PCA per ancestry on LD-pruned variants (plink2 --indep-pairwise 200 50 0.2, then --pca 20 exact) — the GTEx convention.
  • Covariates: per ancestry × modality, first-5 genotype PCs + HCP factors 1–k* (k* selected per ancestry × modality by module 25b, chr1 eGene maximization on each modality’s own HCPs) + sex + gestational age + cell-type fractions (Syncytiotrophoblast as reference). The maternal cell-fraction covariate (ct_Maternal) is excluded BEFORE pruning by analysis decision (coded --exclude-covariates); the remaining pool is correlation-pruned (iterative max-|r| > 0.9 removal, protecting sex/GA > PCs > cell types > HCPs — correlated HCPs are dropped, so effective k can fall below nominal k*) with no covariate cap (details and QC below).
  • Mapping (tensorQTL, cis window ±1 Mb): (i) per-modality grouped — all phenotypes of a gene within a modality tested as one group (permutation-calibrated gene-level p-value; the row label is the driver phenotype); (ii) combined — all phenotypes of a gene across all modalities as one cross-modality group (PANTRY’s headline design); (iii) ungrouped — per-phenotype lead variants for transcript-level resolution; (iv) stepwise (cis.map_independent) for conditionally independent signals, entered at FDR ≤ 5%.
  • Multiple testing: Storey q-values on the permutation-calibrated p-value (pval_beta), computed with the R qvalue package (default lambda) — the GTEx convention, and statistically identical to tensorQTL’s own calculate_qvalues. (On this cluster the rpy2/conda-R route to qvalue hits an unresolvable libstdc++/GLIBCXX conflict, so q-values are computed through a file-based bridge to the singularity R container used elsewhere in the pipeline.)

Covariate correlation matrices before/after pruning: no |r| > 0.9 pairs remain in the final sets.

2.3 Sample attrition

Of the 606 RNA-seq libraries entering the pipeline (605 Salmon-quantified), 420 individuals were retained through QTL mapping — 280 EAS and 140 EUR — after QC, ancestry assignment, genotype intersection, and PCA-outlier removal.

2.4 HCP count optimization (module 25b)

Module 25b estimates HCPs from each modality’s own harmonized matrix at candidate k = 0–30 (step 5) on the pruned fixed covariate set (no cap), maps a chr1 phenotype subset per k, and selects k* by eGene yield with ties to the smaller k; every ancestry × modality run then mapped with its own matched covariate set. Chosen k* span 5–30 across the 20 ancestry × modality cells (table above). The spread is the scientifically important result: EUR splicing and intron retention optimize at k = 5, far below the EUR expression optimum (k = 15), and the EUR splicing layer — which carried no detectable signal under expression-derived covariates — yields 500 FDR ≤ 5% eGenes with splicing-matched factors (Results). EAS splicing is the counterpoint: eGene yield is flat across its entire grid (≤ 3 chr1 eGenes at every k), so its near-null result is robust to HCP specification rather than a consequence of it.

Splicing splits by ancestry: EUR splicing reaches the q ≤ 0.05 tier (500 eGenes with splicing-matched covariates), while EAS splicing remains near-null — best q-value 0.0026 — so the EAS splicing bar sits almost entirely in the q > 0.50 tier.

3.3 Phenotypes per gene group (PANTRY Fig 2b adapted)

Stepwise regression (cis.map_independent) ran on 10316 FDR-qualifying groups; 893 group(s) carry a conditionally independent secondary signal (rank ≥ 2). The design-level view below shows how many phenotypes each gene contributes to its group (the multiple-testing unit).

Combined groups integrate a median of ~4–5 phenotypes per gene (max > 100) — the cross-modality burden-sharing the PANTRY design exploits. (Stability shows a flat box at 1 by design: one phenotype per gene.)

4 Calibration and diagnostics

4.1 Permutation-calibrated p-value QQ plots

Two reference points calibrate the reading. EAS splicing — the lowest-signal layer (a handful of FDR ≤ 5% hits) — departs from the diagonal only mildly (genomic-control λ at the median = 1.28), while every signal-bearing layer, EUR splicing now included (λ = 1.81), departs upward broadly and early with λ at the median of 1.37–2.7 — the expected QQ signature when a substantial fraction of tests are true associations (Storey π1 up to 41%; below). The EAS splicing curve is the calibration control: technical inflation from the shared mapping machinery would bend it like the signal-bearing layers, and it is instead the flattest curve on the plot — the calibration is honest where signal is weakest, and the EUR splicing departure matches the signature of its FDR-significant catalog rather than of artifact.

π1 estimates are 6–41% across all cells, with the largest fractions in EUR RNA_editing grouped and EUR combined combined. Storey q-values diverge from BH exactly where they should: in high-π1 cells the estimated π0 < 1 deflates q-values relative to BH (max |q − BH| across the combined layer = 0.55, at the null end of the ranked list where BH q-values approach 1). At the FDR ≤ 5% boundary the π0 lift admits 1330 vs 1079 (EAS) and 2187 vs 1624 (EUR) combined-layer eGenes for Storey vs BH — the expected, principled gain from estimating the null fraction rather than assuming π0 = 1.

At n ≈ 140 (EUR), only xQTLs explaining ≳ 19% of phenotype variance are detectable at genome-wide thresholds; the larger EAS stratum (n ≈ 280) brings the floor to ≈ 10% — versus ≈ 6% at PANTRY’s n = 445. For reference, PANTRY (n = 445) reported 6,798 eGenes and a 66% discovery gain from non-expression modalities; GTEx tissues at n ≈ 150 typically report hundreds to ~2,000 eGenes. The yield (14959 FDR ≤ 5% associations; 3517 combined-layer eGenes) sits within that range.

The MAC ≥ 5 floor is applied at the genotype intersection in module 23 (before outlier exclusion). A fraction of tests retain < 5 carriers in the mapping sample sets (audit table) because the floor predates outlier exclusion and modality-specific sample attrition. No FDR-significant result should be carrier-limited; hit lists should be post-filtered to ma_count ≥ 5, and re-applying the floor after outlier exclusion would remove them at the source.

8 Transcript-level driver resolution

The combined layer labels each gene-group by its driver phenotype (the phenotype with the best nominal association in the group), and the ungrouped layer provides per-phenotype lead variants. Applied to the FDR-significant catalog, this resolves which modality and transcript carries each eGene signal.

9 Biological interpretation

The discovery landscape: 14959 FDR ≤ 5% associations — 1330 EAS and 2187 EUR eGenes in the primary combined-layer catalog (n ≈ 280/140, MAF ≥ 0.01 + MAC ≥ 5, genome-wide permutation calibration). Strongest per ancestry: EAS: PGM1 (expression, grouped layer, q = 6.1e-26, r² ≈ 0.18); EUR: ERAP1 (alt_polyA, ungrouped layer, q = 5.6e-36, r² ≈ 0.45). Hit effect sizes (r² 0.00–0.77) sit in the class the power floor permits. All hits should be treated as candidates: visual QC of phenotype levels by genotype and replication in larger placental cohorts come before functional claims.

Three characterization observations:

  1. Modality composition. expression leads the EAS grouped-eGene breakdown (1111 of 2410); isoform_expression leads the EUR grouped-eGene breakdown (1356 of 4019) PANTRY’s central finding was that non-expression modalities carry the largest share of regulatory signal; the driver-modality composition of the catalog (above) tests whether that ordering holds in placenta.
  2. Ancestry sharing. 595 of 1328 EAS and 2184 EUR combined-layer eGenes are shared (Fisher OR 4.87, p = 2.1e-135 vs the tested-in-both universe). Shared eGenes are the cross-ancestry replication signal; specific sets are candidates for ancestry-biased regulation.
  3. Functional enrichment. Top g:Profiler term per set: EAS combined eGenes — Metabolic pathways (KEGG, g:SCS p = 0.0018); EUR combined eGenes — Post-translational modification: synthesis of GPI-anchored proteins (REAC, g:SCS p = 0.00061); shared eGenes — Neutrophil degranulation (REAC, g:SCS p = 7.4e-05). Full tables in tables/enrichment_*.tsv.

9.1 Literature context

Positive control: the ERAP1/ERAP2 locus (5q15). The strongest signal shared across ancestries is ERAP2 — a top-10 combined-layer gene in both strata (EAS #6, q = 1.1×10⁻¹⁹, expression driver; EUR #4, q = 7.2×10⁻²⁹, isoform-expression driver) — with ERAP1 the #1 gene in EUR (q = 3.3×10⁻³¹, alt_polyA driver). ERAP2 is a canonical preeclampsia risk locus: fetal-genome variants at ERAP2 associate with preeclampsia in Australian/Norwegian (Johnson et al. 2009), Brazilian (Ferreira et al. 2021), and African American (Hill et al. 2011) cohorts, and ERAP1/ERAP2 are differentially expressed in preeclamptic placentas (Seamon et al. 2020). The EUR driver being isoform expression is mechanism-consistent: the preeclampsia-associated ERAP2 variation tags a haplotype under balancing selection whose molecular effect is alternative splicing and nonsense-mediated decay of ERAP2 transcripts (Andrés et al. 2010; Raja & Kuiper 2023; Ye et al. 2018) — exactly the phenotype class our isoform-expression layer measures. Recovering this locus, through the expected modality, is direct evidence that the atlas captures disease-relevant placental regulation.

Top combined-layer genes, per ancestry. EAS: the top signal is an uncharacterized lncRNA (ENSG00000290199, q = 3.7×10⁻²³) — a novel candidate with no annotation; PGM1 (#2, expression driver) — placental phosphoglucomutase activity is long established (Fazi et al. 1990) and PGM1 loss disrupts cellular energy homeostasis (Conte et al. 2023), relevant to placental glycogen handling in diabetic pregnancy (Lafta et al. 2021); FBLN1 (#3, isoform-expression driver) — fibulin-1 functions in placentation (Singh et al. 2006), placental ECM remodeling in late-onset preeclampsia (García-Montero et al. 2026), and maternal plasma fibulin-1 tracking pregnancy progression (Orvik et al. 2021); IQCG (#4, expression driver) — ciliary/flagellar function with no prior placental association (novel candidate); PSCA (#5, alt_polyA driver) — overexpressed in gestational trophoblastic neoplasia (Feng et al. 2007); RPS28 (#7, expression driver) — small-subunit ribosomal protein with no prior placental association (novel candidate); TOR1AIP1 (#8, isoform-expression driver) — the LAP1 nuclear-envelope protein; biallelic loss causes multisystemic nuclear envelopathy with growth retardation (Fichtman et al. 2019; reviewed in Mackels et al. 2023), with no prior placental association; SPSB2 (#9, expression driver) — an E3-ligase adaptor targeting iNOS for proteasomal degradation (Kuang et al. 2010; Li et al. 2021), placing it in nitric-oxide biology central to placental vascular function; MRPL43 (#10, intron-retention driver) — a mitoribosomal protein already known to carry an antagonistic cis-eQTL acting oppositely on transcription and translation (Han & Lee 2022), and fellow mitoribosomal subunit MRPL13 drives trophoblast mitochondrial stress in early-onset preeclampsia (Chen et al. 2026); ELP5 (#11, alt_polyA driver) — an Elongator-complex subunit required for tRNA wobble-uridine modification (Huang et al. 2005), no prior placental association; THNSL2 (#12, expression driver) — no prior placental association (novel candidate). EUR: ERAP1 (#1) and ERAP2 (#4) above; ZSCAN9 (#2, expression driver) — KRAB zinc-finger with no prior placental association (novel candidate); CTNND1 (#3, RNA-editing driver) — p120-catenin is required for trophoblast proliferation and lineage specification at implantation (Qin et al. 2024) and sits in the Wnt-regulated invasion program (Knöfler & Pollheimer 2013); CTSB (#5, RNA-editing driver) — cathepsin B, whose serum level is elevated in preeclampsia and tracks disease severity (Kim et al. 2016; Park et al. 2020); STBD1 (#6, expression driver) — the glycophagy receptor linking glycogen to selective autophagy (Zhang et al. 2024; Tang et al. 2023), a second glycogen-metabolism hit alongside PGM1; APIP (#7, stability driver) — an anti-apoptotic Apaf-1 inhibitor protective under hypoxia/ischemia (Cho et al. 2004) that is also the methionine-salvage enzyme mtnB (Mary et al. 2012) — a plausible hypoxia-response link to placental biology; WDR91 (#8, expression driver) — a Rab7 effector in endolysosomal trafficking (Rapiteanu et al. 2016; Ma et al. 2024), no prior placental association; MEAK7 (#9, expression driver) — an mTORC1-associated protein; trophoblast mTOR signaling controls placental nutrient transport and fetal growth (Shao et al. 2021; Rosario et al. 2025); ARFGAP3 (#10, isoform-expression driver) — COPI vesicle-coat assembly at the Golgi (Kartberg et al. 2010), no prior placental association; GBP3 (#11, isoform-expression driver) — an interferon-inducible GTPase in cell-autonomous immunity (Tretina et al. 2019; Kirkby et al. 2023), no prior placental association; KANSL1-AS1 (#12, expression driver) — placental expression of this lncRNA tracks infant birthweight in the GAPPS cohort (Hussey et al. 2025).

Modality-matched covariates, in line with QTL practice. Latent-factor covariates are a standard power lever in QTL mapping (Stegle et al. 2012), and splicing layers — quantified annotation-free from intron usage (Li et al. 2017) — have hidden structure that need not track gene expression. The per-modality HCP choice behaved as that practice predicts: EUR splicing was null under expression-derived factors and recovers 500 eGenes at its own k* = 5, while the EAS splicing null is flat across the entire k grid, excluding covariate specification as its cause.

Sub-threshold top-ranked genes (tables above) remain prioritization hints only — and the flagged low-carrier rows should be discounted outright.

10 Limitations and next steps

  1. Power. n ≈ 280/140 with a ~12k-gene testing burden detects only r² ≳ 0.10 (EAS) / 0.19 (EUR) effects. Doubling n would roughly halve the detectable r²; matching PANTRY’s n = 445 would bring the floor to ≈ 0.06. Adding the remaining cohorts and the AFR/AMR/SAS strata is the highest-value next step.
  2. EAS splicing is near-null. The layer yields a handful of FDR ≤ 5% eGenes while EUR splicing — at a higher detection floor — yields 500. The EAS result is robust to HCP count (flat k-grid), so covariate specification is excluded as the cause; the leading candidate is cross-cohort heterogeneity in junction-level quantification (EAS pools four cohorts spanning single- and paired-end protocols). Revisiting splicing quantification harmonization across the EAS cohorts, and adding EAS cohorts, are the targeted next steps.
  3. Technical replicates. 25 mapped individuals (4 EAS, 21 EUR) have two RNA-seq runs. Phenotype values come from the single ComBat-processed run per individual, while run-level covariates (cell-type fractions, QC metrics) are averaged across the pair — a slight phenotype/covariate misalignment for those individuals. Future runs will collapse replicates at the count level before batch correction so phenotypes and covariates are averaged consistently, with a pre-collapse replicate-concordance QC gate.
  4. Carrier-count propagation. The MAC ≥ 5 floor predates outlier exclusion, so low-carrier tests persist in some mapping outputs (audit table above). No reported result depends on them; hit lists should post-filter to ma_count ≥ 5, and re-applying the floor after outlier exclusion would remove them at the source.
  5. Ancestry asymmetry. EUR tests more phenotypes than EAS in every modality (ancestry-specific filtering), so cross-ancestry comparisons are restricted to genes tested in both.
  6. No pooled cross-ancestry inference was performed. If combined discovery is wanted later, Fisher/Stouffer or an inverse-variance slope meta-analysis are the clean options.
  7. Stepwise secondary signals: 893 groups carry a conditionally independent secondary signal (table above).
  8. Fine-mapping and colocalization are out of scope. The natural follow-ups on the FDR-significant catalog are SuSiE fine-mapping per eGene locus, GWAS colocalization (coloc/eCAVIAR) against placental and pregnancy-outcome GWAS, and locus-zoom visual QC of each hit (nominal-scan extraction + LD from the ancestry-matched genotype panel).
  9. Replication path: the FDR-significant hits are the priorities for lookup in larger placental resources or a future meta-analysis; visual QC of phenotype levels by genotype is the immediate sanity check for each.

11 Reproducibility

  • Results: tensorQTL cis mapping (grouped / ungrouped / combined / stepwise), MAF ≥ 0.01 + MAC ≥ 5 at the genotype intersection, ±1 Mb window, Storey q-values on pval_beta via the R qvalue package (singularity-R bridge). Covariates: as described (first-5 PCs + HCP_1–k* + sex/GA/cell types; maternal fraction excluded before correlation pruning; no cap). Genotype PCs: cohort-only plink2 PCA on LD-pruned variants.
  • Pipeline scripts: this repository (05_qtl_mapping/, scripts 19–30 + compute_qvalues.R; genotype pooling in 01_genotype_imputation/).
  • Report code: report_placenta_xqtl.Rmd + xqtl_report_functions.R; figures in figures/, tables in tables/.
  • Gene symbols: gene_map.tsv regenerated in full from the normalized GTF (config normalized_gtf) by make_report_archive.sh at archive time — covers every tested gene, version-stripped IDs.
